## LLM009 HTTP client without a timeout

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Level | warning |
| Framework | Both |
| Autofix | no patch; fix it by hand as described below |
| More | https://pgy763.github.io/llm-dev-pitfalls/java/Reactor超时截断流式 |
| Turn it off | `LLM009: off` in .llm-lint.yml, or `--disable LLM009` on the command line |

An HTTP client with no timeout waits forever by default. If the peer never answers, the request thread hangs, and the thread pool fills up first.

To mute it in one place, put `// llm-lint:ignore LLM009` on that line or the line above.
<!-- /generated:llm009 -->

## What it looks like

A `@Bean` returning `RestClient` / `WebClient` / `HttpClient` / `RestTemplate` built without a timeout.

## How to fix

Set connect and read timeouts explicitly, a few seconds each. The defaults are effectively infinite and park threads under load.
